claims.not_probed_reason: The new evidence resolves the operational date anchor: SAP page 9 places randomization at Visit 3 and Define-XML sources ADSL.TRTSDT from SV.SVSTDTC at that visit. A collected-assessment window calculation can therefore use published upstream ADT minus published ADSL.TRTSDT, without silently applying ADY's post-reference +1 or reading the derived exposure-based ADSL output. The remaining whole-variable limitation is applicability to created LOCF recipient records: the citable documents specify assessment-date windowing, targeted donor assessments and the recipient analysis schedule, but do not independently identify created rows or state a complete recipient-visit assignment while donor dates are retained. Applying donor-date windows globally would assume recipient labels follow donor windows; exempting selected rows or mapping the preserved AVISITN back to AVISIT would instead assume or reuse the target visit. DTYPE identifies imputation use, not an independently documented created-row discriminator. No partial-scope or target-encoding probe is claimed as a whole-variable literal. The exact-section baseline text additionally loses the native PDF equality underline: the original is <=1, and a strict <1 probe from extracted text would misrepresent it. This representation caveat is not a baseline conflict.
interpretations: The exact citable SAP page-11 text reads "3 Baseline < 1 1". The original retained SAP.pdf physical page 11 (printed page 10), Section 8.2, ADAS-Cog/CIBIC+ table, visibly has an underlined less-than sign, meaning <=1. Inspect cdiscpilot01/spec/source/SAP.pdf#page=11 or .build/extraction/adqsadas1-sap-window.png. This is a PDF-to-text boundary artifact, not evidence of a confirmed document/spec baseline discrepancy. The formal quote is retained without silently changing it.

SAP page 9 and Define-XML ADSL.TRTSDT together provide a faithful operational randomization anchor: the Visit-3 SV start date, available through published ADSL.TRTSDT. This conclusion uses the protocol/source chain rather than equating randomization and dosing by their labels. SAP's AVISIT day remains visit date minus that anchor; separately documented ADY adds one on or after TRTSDT. Those different quantities do not themselves contradict the ADY documentation. The AVISIT probe must isolate this rule using upstream published inputs, not the current derived ADSL file.
The scheduled-visit numbers in SAP are CRF visit identifiers; the output analysis-visit numeric codes come from the AVISITN codelist.

The ordinary obs branch windows each assessment date. The added locf8, locf16 and locf24 branches instead assign the recipient labels Week 8, Week 16 and Week 24 while retaining donor ADT, ADY, VISIT and VISITNUM. The SAP supports LOCF analyses at those recipient visits, but does not fully operationalize which published target records are created recipients or how that row distinction should be independently recovered for a date-window probe. DTYPE=LOCF also occurs on ordinary rows when their AVAL changes, so treating every imputed row as a synthetic recipient would add a false discriminator. REF.AVISITN is the target visit's numeric encoding and cannot independently establish AVISIT.

Native retained upstream implementation pointer: cdiscpilot01/spec/yamaa/adsl.yaml, EX_MINDTC and TRTSDT (around lines 384-407), and cdiscpilot01/spec/yamaa/adqsadas.yaml input ADSL plus column TRTSDT. ADQSADAS reads adsl-yamaa.parquet; upstream TRTSDT uses MIN(EX.EXSTDTC) and date imputation despite a metadata comment naming SV Visit 3. That implementation pointer explains the executable-source clauses; it is not a substitute formal document quotation or a measured equality/difference of the submitted dates.

Any eventual probe must retain original matching columns STUDYID, USUBJID, PARAMCD, AVISITN and QSSEQ unchanged. It must not copy REF.AVISIT, invert REF.AVISITN as proof of its own label, use REF.ADY as SAP calendar difference, or introduce a first/last raw-date or missing-input default unsupported by the documents. New helpers would use _ADAS_FU_ names.
claims.assessment: The retained protocol and source definition now identify a faithful operational Visit-3 date anchor. The executable chain uses the separately documented ADY arithmetic and derived upstream exposure date. A complete whole-variable literal still requires an independently specified application of date windows versus recipient labels across created LOCF records; the native inclusive baseline remains an exact-section representation caveat. Pilot 6's R reimplementation windows collected records on ADY (adadas.r L69-L75, with the baseline window ADY <= 1) and takes the visit of created ACTOT LOCF records from its expected-visit table (L117-L123) through derive_locf_records (L125-L139), which carries donor ADT and ADY (L136); it thus assigns the recipient visit from the expected schedule rather than from donor dates.
claims.question: What retained rule independently identifies created LOCF recipient records and assigns their recipient analysis visit when donor ADT/VISIT is retained?
